messages:
olivia: quick q — ACME POC requires a fully air-gapped on-prem install. Can we outline packaging options, upgrade cadence choices, and the license/activation story? cc @dmitri @rachel

dmitri: we can do a couple of delivery formats: OCI image tar (preferred for containerized single-vm) or a tarball with binaries for a sysd service. For k8s we ship an offline helm bundle. For strict airgap OCI tar + install script is the safest.

rachel: two recommended tracks: (1) single-vm installer (systemd + containerd) for quick POC, (2) full k8s helm offline bundle for customers who run clusters. All artifacts signed and SHA256-verified.

olivia: ACME specifically asked for single-vm first — they have strict network rules and no cluster.

dmitri: single-vm flow looks like: deliver redwood-offline-<ver>.tar.gz that contains images and an install shim. Example install:
```sh
sudo tar -xvf redwood-offline-1.3.0.tar.gz -C /opt/redwood
sudo ./install.sh --offline
```
The installer imports images into containerd and configures systemd units.

jin: security notes: artifacts must be signed and we provide reproducible hashes. They asked about KMS/HSM — we support customer-managed KMS integrations and can run HSM-based key wraps; need integration test if they use a nonstandard vendor.

ops: upgrade cadence options we can offer: monthly security patches, quarterly feature releases, or a 12-month LTS channel. For airgap upgrades we support full bundle upgrades and delta patches (smaller payloads). Expect a small maintenance window for DB migrations (5-15m typical for medium datasets).

rachel: migrations are transactional for minor changes; major upgrades require approval and may need a longer window. We provide a rollback plan for patch-level upgrades.

olivia: is there a pricing delta for airgapped packaging/private builds?

dmitri: yes — there's a one-time packaging + signing fee to cover private build and artifact signing pipeline. Also recommend Dedicated support SLA for fast patch churn. I'll hand over numbers to sales, but call it a non-recurring packaging charge + monthly support.

olivia: they also want upgrade automation. They asked: can upgrades be applied via removable media (USB) or must they push to an internal registry?

rachel: both supported. USB workflow: copy OCI tar + run install.sh. Internal-registry workflow: import with `ctr image import` or push to their airgapped registry. We'll include both runbook snippets.

dmitri: constraints to call out: supported OS: RHEL 8/9 and Ubuntu 20.04/22.04. No Windows. SELinux enforced is tested. FIPS-enabled builds are available but add 2–3 weeks lead time. Also time sync (NTP) required for cert verification in airgapped envs.

jin: they will need an SBOM and third-party lib list for their security questionnaire. That takes ~2 weeks to assemble with legal sign-off. Also need to document offline vulnerability scanning process.

olivia: can someone craft a short POC runbook? ACME wants a 2-week POC with an upgrade exercise.

rachel: will draft: Day0 install, Day2 smoke tests, Day5 scale/load, Day9 upgrade test, Day13 rollback/handoff. I'll put it into Confluence and share the link here.

ops: created internal task for tracking packaging work — deploy-bot: Created task RED-PAK-1234 for airgap packaging and delivery.

dmitri: main technical blockers: FIPS validation and any uncommon HSM integrations. If they require FIPS + vendor-specific HSM testing, add 2–3 weeks. Otherwise we can do install + upgrade POC in ~1 week (install + 1 upgrade test week).

olivia: awesome. I'll sync timeline and confirm whether they need FIPS/HSM vendor details. @rachel please add pricing line items for: packaging fee, Dedicated airgap support, optional FIPS validation.

rachel: on it — will share a draft quote and the POC runbook later today.
